resources.string: There you are. I won't waste time on courtesies. I want your help with an investigation.
"Isn't that your specialty? Why me?"
One, you're effective, quite more than Alecksi bargained for. Two, you're loyal, which gives you the motivation to help me.
"I don't really care about you."
But you do care about Cecilia. Settle your hackles, it's not a threat. She's taking the throne, but what happens without support from the major Houses?
"So I help you, and you support her?"
And I become unofficially friendly to her agenda. Start your investigation with Lucian. He's had an eye on my seat, and not in any interesting way.
Have you made progress? I want results, not empty speculation.
You hear something?
Jumpy?
Wouldn't you be? Matter of time before "She" finds out about Lucian's operation.
Stupid, hiding things from Carmilla. That human must be important if Lucian doesn't trust you lot with the cell key.
Quit prying, idiot! You want the Feeders down there on you, too? Let's go.
Apologies if you were expecting someone far less intelligent. That would be my fellow scholar Sabine, who unfortunately was not captured in my stead.
"You're awfully pleasant."
Oh please forgive me, if my being tortured by sadistic monstrosities has hampered my ability to pretend I like you!
In any case, we'd best get going. I overheard my tormentors bragging that they plan to ambush Sabine and Cecilia in Bitu Umbre.
"Who's Sabine?"
Oh, I do so love to repeat myself. I am Kisher, a scholar from the Archives. Sabine is also a scholar, still with me? Sabine found dangerous information which-
"Why were you meeting Cecilia?"
I was against it! We're scholars, not politicians. But Sabine claimed, hysterically, that some information she'd unearthed could affect "all humans in Nighthaven."
"And among the Upyr..."
Yes, Cecilia is the most sympathetic toward humans. I've mentally upgraded you from imbecile to proficient in basic reasoning. You're welcome.
Oh no, I don't despise Sabine. Do I look down on her? Am I jealous of the Sage King's stupefyingly illogical favoritism toward her? Also no.
Well? Was I right? Was it Lucian?
"It was Lucian."
Ha! I didn't think he had it in him. Well done. But there's something else, something you're not telling me. Oh it's all right. For now. I'll be watching you.
Thank the gods you're safe. I'm glad Kisher here, was able to rescue you from Lucian's prisons.
I may have- decorated the truth a bit.
Gisiv Yolliw Zigozih Rih Zi Nizik…
It's her mind, they've broken her. The assassins overwhelmed my guard, but when the battle turned, the cowards targeted Sabine and fled.
"Why target a scholar?"
She deciphered an ancient tome- the Blood Atlas, and found a way to adapt its powerful shielding magic for humans to use. Though, without the proper key-
-the book was destroyed! So they targeted her for her knowledge. If humans could shield their souls, their mana, they could resist the Upyr.
All the more reason we must recover her mind. Why are you all staring at me as if I'd gone mad?
"You're an Upyr."
Subjugating others isn't just wrong, it's stupid. Now. With Founding Day coming, we can meet in Tularest without drawing attention. But how do we heal Sabine?
She's quoting from the Blood Atlas. I think her mind somehow- retreated, into the book. If I could get the Sun Key that unlocks the Atlas, it may help.
"I'll get the key."
Thank you. Kisher clearly doesn't think you can win past the tombs, but he doesn't know you. We regroup in Tularest Abbey. Seek out Lord Galbrion, he owes me.
It's not just important to save Sabine for the good of human and Upyr society. She trusted me. I won't let her down.
Ah, the Sun Key. I feel- yes! Slightly less miserable. All these sky-staring fools yammering about, how does anyone manage to think? They don't, that's the answer!
Yes something is bothering me! For here in Tularest, resides the prime example of everything worst about the puffed up Upyr nobles.
"Lord Galbrion?"
Excellent if obvious guess. I need medicine to calm Sabine, and he's "too busy." Busy kissing every mirror he comes across, apparently. Would you talk to him?
Any luck with that vomitious pufftato Lord Galbrion? I know, I made up those words, now leave me be.
And if I don't get my feast supplies back immediately, I shall reallocate funds meant to feed the unwashed monkeys otherwise known as humans.
"The scholar sent me to-"
To waste more of my time! Get in line, I shan't be long, I'm just waiting to hear the soothing dyad of submission and servile flattery from Mayor Bogdan here.
Great Lord Galbrion- I so look forward to Tularest Founding Day in which we celebrate your magnificent rise to Governor. But the Berlaur are too powerful for us-
But-but-but-but- always excuses! "But we need to eat, we need clean water to drink, we need clothes! We're too weak to fight werebeasts!"
"I'll do it- for the medicine."
You see, Mayor! "I will do it." That is how humans should properly answer their Upyr masters. All right, I'll bring the medicine around for your friend Sabiney.
Soulwarden! What a pleasant surprise, what brings you to Tularest? And with all those bags of supplies?
"Lord Galbrion requested help."
Nonsense! No, no, the ah, the Soulwarden volunteered-
The Soulwarden is no page to order about, Lord Galbrion. We'll speak about this later. At length.
Soulwarden, you may recall Lynette. She came here chasing rumors, and sadly was just leaving.
"Maybe Lynette can help."
Oh I've seen well enough how she "helps," seen it all my life as she practiced "helping" my father with her honeyed tongue to do everything that she willed.
If you're quite done, Cece.
I am your Queen, Lynette! You will speak to me with due respect!
Queen Cecilia. Please. I know there's something huge going on, something that could shake the Upyr's grip on humankind. I'll do anything to help.
"I trust her."
Hahh. I'm sure I'll regret this. Sabine is a scholar from the Archives. She found a way for humans to use Blood Atlas shielding magic, but her mind was ravaged.
With the Sun Key, we have a chance for recovery. The Blood Atlas protects her mind, but is at the same time a prison. If we enact the Ritual to unlock the Atlas-
We unlock her mind. Soulwarden, you're the best fighter here. We'll need the Chalice of We-ila, and- Upyr ichor. We meet at Memora Singur to start the Ritual.
The Devils howl at night. Hide the Empress in the Castles!
Have you seen the way Lynette sidles up to Lord Galbrion? Well I have. It reminds me too much of things I'd rather forget.
It's not working, is it? There's something missing.
"Could've told me earlier."
But then I wouldn't have been able to see your ridiculous confused face. Don't hit me! It's the activation jewels!
There's a red, green, and blue gem for each control post. Slot them in there and the device should be ready to go.
I'm- who are you? What's happened?
"Do you remember anything?"
I- I remember meeting with Cecilia and then the- ouch! My head. There was something important- something I was to remember- but it's gone. I'm sorry.
Foolish girl! I told you meddling in all this nonsense would do us no good! I'll take her back to the Archives, let her recover someplace familiar.
If anything changes, let us know immediately! It's more important than you could ever imagine.
That's quite enough, Lynette. We're just glad she's back. Soulwarden, yet again, I can't thank you enough. I'd stay, but- things are- not quite settled at home.
I've something to speak with you about, Soulwarden. At Lord Galbrion's place in Tularest. Meet you there?
I'll speak plainly. Cecilia needs help. She's just starting to realize that she can't step into her father's shoes so easily. The old nobles don't respect her yet.
"Lord Galbrion does."
Oh- well, I've always been-
Afraid? There there, m'Lord, you've got a healthy sense of self-preservation. Now. There is a Challenge system where Champions can prove their worth-
"So Houses can safely declare?"
You catch on quick. But- as Galbrion is itching to say, major Houses won't issue their Challenges to you now. You need to build your reputation first, earn favor.
"I can do that."
Good. Speak with Alice or Fabian if you need supplies, we'll set them up to assist. I'll be here as well if you need me.
You're staying here? In my- in my quarters?
Oh! How generous of you! I accept! See you around, Soulwarden. Lord Galbrion or I will send word if anything urgent comes up.
You're here! Good work, word's going around that Cecilia has a powerful new Champion. But there's something else- we've captured a communique from Lucian.
"He's still intact?"
Perhaps not completely so. My spies tell me Lady Carmilla's had several- "Feeder" sessions with him in the dungeons. Which is why I think he slipped up.
But why would Lucian warn the Inquisitors he'd been compromised? The Inquisitors don't work with anyone but the Inquisitors. I believe you're too hopeful.
Stop being such a sniveling coward, Lord Galbrion! I'm sorry. But the Upyr high nobles aren't as clever as you think. They've given us a chance to unmask them.
"I'll check it out."
Nice to know someone here who isn't a mouse. Still, be careful out there. The Inquisitors aren't to be trifled with. I've got the scars to prove it.
Much as I hate to admit it, there is something suspicious about the Inquisitors being involved. But we really don't have the luxury to sit back and worry.
It was a trap? Oh, goodness, that's simply awful! Do you think- do you think I'm in danger? Do you think they know I'm helping you and Lynette?
"Do you suspect Lynette?"
What? No, I mean tedious, annoying, yes, but aren't all humans really, and though she does tend to disappear rather suddenly, enthralled? I don't think so.
Let's keep our collective eyes open, he whispered huskily. For now, keep working on your reputation, we're almost there! Ugh. Being supportive. Makes me ill.
Unbelievably, you've done it. House Bathory has taken notice and are issuing a formal Challenge. Though, being the House of War, I don't expect it'll go easily.
"Where's Lynette?
Exactly! One wonders, he said as he stared at the letter Lynette read before running out of the room almost in tears. Ahem. Read. The letter.
Be wary around Lynette- I know I said before that I didn't suspect her but- at the very least she's been quite- strained, recently.
Well? A monkey could've penned better, no? Though I didn't expect Lynette's "spies" to be intelligent, this one couldn't even spell. "Iron CRONE?" "Night WELL?"
"She's going to Cronewell."
Ha! Oh! Oh. You mean- it was some kind of code? Crone. Well. Of course! I knew that. Let you figure it out on your own. But remember, the Challenge comes first.
"Lynette comes first."
This is why I can't stand working with humans! Do you know how hard we've worked to gain a House Challenge? If we don't bolster- you're not listening are you?
You must be the Soulwarden. I am Bianca, from House Bathory. I've come to-
"Issue a House Challenge?"
You're well informed, Ser. The Lord wishes to communicate his regret that he could not invite you in person. He seems quite interested in you, if I'm to be honest.
"And you?"
As interested as a servant of the Upyr may allow herself. And now I've said too much. Godspeed, Soulwarden. There are many who wish you well.
Why allow us to bear weapons? Because they think us little threat, and because we cannot go against their will once they've- fed upon our mana.
Soulwarden. How did you find me? Well, I suppose I have a lot to answer for. Selfish of me to be out here, I know.
"How is your- friend?"
Being careful. Sparing my feelings. You sometimes remind me of Everard. I loved him, once, and he never stopped loving me. I think I saw him- inside. Would you?
"I'll look for him."
Thank you. And- if you have to- put him to rest. Please do it.
Was it him? Was it Everard?
"Yes, I think so. I found this."
Gods, that hurts. We came to Aeternum together, he, my sister, and I. We called him "little lion" because whenever we caught him lying, he'd say "just a little."
"I'm sorry for your loss."
They just keep coming, don't they? The losses. Oh! But what news on the Houses? We must line up support for Cecilia, and fast. Our enemies grow bolder.
"Bathory's issued challenge."
What? Seriously? That's incredible! House Bathory is one of the most influential in Nighthaven! With their support- go already! I'll be fine. Just need some time.
Well done, Champion! I must admit, I had my doubts. It's no simple matter to take down as many as five spiders in so little time.
"Five? Try fifteen."
What? No, that's impossible! I mean, even I would have trouble with fifteen. Someone must have tampered with the range. But that magic is ancient, complex-
Nonetheless, the Champion has prevailed. I shall declare for Cecilia. I've a soft spot for her anyway, always knew she'd be a better leader.
I've recently spoken with Lynette. I'm sorry, things have been busy and I'd no idea she'd roped you in to helping me yet again. Well, I had some.
"I'm glad to help."
If you're trying to curry favor with the Queen? By all means, do so. But have a care. With Bathory's support, our enemies will grow desperate.
Yes, there are more lines on my face and more gray hairs. If I said Bathory's support would make things easier, you can slap me. But there's good news, too.
"Galbrion's fired?"
Nothing THAT good. But I won't spoil the surprise. Read the letter. Oh never mind I'll tell you- and yes I read it. It's a Challenge from House Carmilla!
I told you the Soulwarden wouldn't understand the significance. In Nighthaven there are two Houses which are the most influential. Bathory and Carmilla-
Meaning, you're amazing! Lady Carmilla also has an extensive spy network. Fortunate, as mine is being rapidly devastated. Our enemy is scared, taking risks.
Let's not count our piglets before they're bacon. Yes I made that up. First the Soulwarden has to win this Challenge. Supportive enthusiasm, et cetera.
Oh, we are close. If we can win House Carmilla's favor- well, if you're able to, that is. Fingers, toes, everything is crossed. Everything.
Oh, you're exciting, aren't you? Crusher of Empires, champion of the weak, conqueror of hearts.
"Is that a confession?"
Oh, dear, that's both interesting and frightening at the same time. All right, let's give it a try shall we? It was a jest. Lower your hackles, Queen Cecilia.
My hackles were never raised. I don't consider you a threat. Not that I care. Ah, blast. So. Ahem. My thanks, Soulwarden.
Well said, my Queen. For a teenager.
Lynette! Ugh. Lady Carmilla, now that we have your support, could we ask your help in unmasking our hidden enemy?
Certainly. But it's vital for our Champion to continue building support, keep pressure on our quarry. I'll be in touch when I find something. Be ready to move quickly.
Was anyone followed? No? We've only one chance at this. Lady Carmilla's discovered who our hidden spy is. Or rather, who it very likely is.
"Even you're not sure?"
Thank you for the faith, Soulwarden. You become more interesting all the time. The spy is in all likelihood, Lord Galbrion.
Galbrion! Damn it! How could I be so naiive- he was right there in front of me, all this time! But how can we be sure it's him?
"We lay a trap."
Yes. We've compromised part of their network, and seeded to spies we know are involved, that Lynette will meet with Cecilia to reveal our enemy's identity.
Just juicy enough, but not so tasty you'd suspect the hook. So if Galbrion shows, we'll know it's him. Remind me never to get on your bad side, Lady Carmilla.
If it's Galbrion I swear I'll pull out every single hair on his face and head, one by one. On just the left side.
If it's Galbrion I swear I'll pull out every single hair on his face and head, one by one. On just the left side.
Someone took our bait! Came skulking around right on time. Didn't get a good look at him though. Ran off that way, soon as you arrived!
You just missed him- he ran off that way!
That bloody arse-kisser Lord Galbrion! I should have known. To think I actually trusted him, makes me feel like the biggest fool ever!
That looked like Galbrion just now!
"It was!"
So it was him! He was running toward his quarters. Carmilla and I were waylaid by assassins, we'll root out the rest and join you. Be careful, he's sure to be desperate!
Soulwarden! I was going to look for Galbrion, when I saw him running in through there! Was it him?
"It was the pufftato himself."
That filthy, greasy faced, self-loving, mirror-licking Upyr Lord! Pufftato? That's brilliant. Now let's find him and kill him a lot. But we need a way in. The door's locked.
The key may be somewhere nearby- ahem- office desk. For example.
Tell us you beat the stuffing out of Galbrion.
"With great pleasure."
Thank you Soulwarden, words simply aren't enough. You're the hope- no, the very Light of Nighthaven-
Would you say a Night- Light? I'm sure you wouldn't mind this one lighting up your nights.
Lynette, I am ordering you to stop teasing me!
Oh but it's so fun! Consider it payment for services rendered to the Queendom.
I hate to interrupt this- whatever it is. But would someone be so kind as to tell me why I've been summoned back to this dreadful hellhole?
Well, Kisher. You know that saying- those who don't want to lead are often the best leaders? We need a new Governor. You understand Upyr and humans.
No no no no! You're joking, right?
"Ha ha ha."
Ha ha ha!
Ha ha ha ha!
Werebeasts, humans. We want the same thing. We want dignity. We want safety. We want freedom from those who take this from us. The Upyr.
(Murmurs of dissent in the crowd.)
The spiders in Grota Caverna are eating people they've captured! How are you any different? You want to prove your Umbra clan is different, rescue them!
Those villagers were captured sneaking into the spiders' caves and plundering gold! For human greed, Berlaur should fight their own? Why?
Because trust is the foundation of the pack! Because trust is the price paid to join hands. And join hands we must to purge Nighthaven of the affliction named Upyr!
Whether what Lyceon wants is truly possible, only time will tell. But a Berlaur must not lead us to take from the spiders, it will start a blood feud.
Razvan is right!
These are but human villagers. And while I respect Razvan's spiritiual guidance-
"I can lead the rescue."
The Soulwarden?! Wonderful! We are grateful for your help. Let this rescue be the first of many times that the Berlaur and humans join hands!
Humans and Berlaur will join hands. It is but a matter of time.
There you are! The spider cave is just down the path. But we can't get through. Aknat and her brood, they overwhelmed us.
"I can draw it away."
Bravely said for a human. All right, let's go with your plan. Draw Aknat deep into the caves and keep him busy. We'll use that chance to get the villagers out.
Well done. Perhaps I judged you too quickly. Thanks to you, we managed to safely rescue all the villagers.
Unfortunately, it seems that we have another issue- at least when it comes to building trust with the humans. I- hesitate to involve you further.
"You can rely on me."
We'll see. Cornelius has something for my father, would you mind picking it up from the forge, on your way to the command post?
I'll meet you by the command post after you've picked up the item for my father.
Ah, the Soulwarden. Ahh. The thing. For Lyceon. It is- here, somewhere.
"So, in this pile?"
Pile? No. This is a collection. A collection.
Ah, you've brought the map. Thank you. Soulwarden, this is my father, Lyceon. Do spare me any comments about a family resemblance.
"I was about to say he's prettier."
Prettier? Are you- Suddenly I don't think sharing our problems with you is very wise.
Ha ha ha! Well done, Soulwarden. I think that's the fastest anyone's gotten under her skin. We'll share our family tale another day. For now, you must be wondering-
"What's going on in Mar Amar."
O ho! Resourceful as well.
Some might call it nosy. I asked you to bring the map, not look at it.
With a snout like mine, I can't call anyone nosy, can I? Soulwarden, we are the Umbra Clan. Our law, our principle, is to never consume human flesh.
"And one of yours did just that."
That's what's being said. Unfortunately, we cannot enter an Upyr-controlled settlement like Mar Amar, to investigate. If you could help Nocturne-
I don't need help, father.
"It'd be my pleasure."
Wonderful! You have my thanks, and my friendship. And I think you will find that we Berlaur are nothing if not loyal.
What do you want? I'm not taking suitors. Especially not from- your kind, no offense.
"I'm here to look into the attacks."
Oh. Well! If you ask me those two ladies had it coming. Loud about town, that's what they were! And the filthy Berlaur! Well you can see their fine work just down the street.
Don't tell me, the Upyr finally sent someone to look into the werebeast attacks?
"Actually the Berlaur sent me."
The Berlaur?! Are you mad? Werebeasts investigating who they'll kidnap next for dinner? Those bastards! Anca- she was good- a good person. Now get you gone!
I seen you- seen you looking around. You're here about the werebeast attacks huh? Am I right? Well I know who did it!
"Who was it?"
A werewolf!
"Uh huh."
I saw it! Big nasty teeth and- it was sneaking into town, same one that got the two ladies! Don't believe me? Go up to the lookout point, you'll see him soon enough!
Did you see him? What did I tell you, it's a werewolf!
And guess what? I saved Beatrice from that beast! It was trying to get into her house! I scared him off and he ran like a coward!
"I'll catch him."
Well go already! Less talk, more walk! He's gonna get away!
I thought myself faster than any human. Seems I was wrong.
Did you get him? Huh?
You are fast, for a human.
"Or you're a slow werewolf."
I would laugh, were it any other occasion.
"Why did you eat the villagers?"
What? Eat them? No! I have not attacked anyone.
"Then why sneak into town?"
I… cannot say. I sense the pack waiting just outside the village. I will turn myself in.
I cannot tell you how disappointed I am in you, Avram. You have brought dishonor to the Umbra Clan's scouts, to Aster, and to the pack.
"He may not be guilty."
Why else would Avram stalk these humans? And he will not speak to defend himself. Aster, as scout master, you will step down and stand tribunal as well.
As you wish, Lyceon.
I do not wish! But we are left with no choice.
I agree with you, Soulwarden. Something's off. Let's try and dig a little deeper, there's a rotten fish buried around here somewhere.
What- what do you want?
"I'm here about the werewolf."
Oh. Well. I don't- I don't know why he was- I mean I don't know him.
"How do you know it's a he?"
Well- they all look like, angry- angry sorts. Will- will he be okay. I mean, I'm okay-
"Thanks to Gariel."
Gariel?! Oh yeah, real godsend that Gariel. Lucky he was near my house? He's always coming by, always pestering me. Well all the women in the village, honestly.
"Know where Gariel lives?"
Just a few houses down. Wish it were a hundred. And you can tell him I said that.
I saw you leap across from the neighboring house. Wasn't going to try that myself. Who lives here?
"Gariel. He's our culprit."
What's this? That's absolutely mad. Seems when he was spurned by his victims, he got rid of them, and staged things to look like werewolf attacks.
"I'm heading out."
To rescue the prior victims? All right. I'll let the others know what's happened. And- thank you.
Thank the gods you're here. That bastard Gariel!
"He left you in here?"
Yes and I'll sink a knife deep in his skull once I get my hands on him. If we ever get out of this tower, that is. It appears we're both stuck now.
"I'll find a way out."
Thank you, please. And once I'm out, I'll make that little weasel-face squeal for mercy.
But it isn't only Anca's word against yours, is it, Gariel? We found some very disturbing letters in your house.
This is all your fault, Anca. If you hadn't rejected me over that stupid Jaris! And Beatrice, cavorting with a dirty mongrel when you could have me!
Avram's ten times the man you'll ever be!
"Let's hand Gariel over to the Upyr."
While I'd like to sink my butcher knives into his skull, I suppose you're right. Let's give the Upyr a new toy to play with.
No, mercy, please- please! Anything but the Upyr!
Justice prevails. Unfortunately yet another crisis has arisen. If- I could ask your help.
"Let's go."
Thank you. I think I owe you an apology, for when we first met. Although you were pretty terrible, yourself.
"Pretty terrible or terribly pretty?"
Just when I started to not dislike you. Come on, let's go.
Every time we step forward with the humans, we slip back another five. Oh I know, I'm human, too, but not on the inside, where it counts.
Ah! Soulwarden! Thank you, for what you've done. You've saved our hides yet again. And yet now we find ourselves weak, poisoned, by the Upyr "reikar."
"What's that?"
Dark Upyr magic. Centuries of Upyr experimenting on captured Berlaur. The reikar distort lunar energy, weaken us. These are strong, we can't even get near.
Well then, we humans just need to step in and help you weak little werebeasts.
Right. They helped us, even when we didn't deserve it. Now it's our turn.
"I'm in too."
Wonderful. I- I am touched. My dream. No, our dream. Thank you, my human friends! My daughter will meet you out there.
Seems like the emitter towers have powered shields- must be an improvement from our Upyr "friend" Baroness Anastasia. Each one has a power source nearby.
"So we take out the power first."
Right! I'll mark your map with the closest power source and emitter pair. Take care of the ones in here. I'll get the ones in the field.
You are a godsend. I hoped for so long that this dream was achievable- and now- look, the humans have actually helped the Berlaur- isn't that amazing?
But now, we must discuss matters of much greater importance.
"Oh, no. What is it now?"
A feast! And you will be our guest of honor! We could not have built this without you, my friend!
Thank you, Soulwarden. You've made my father very happy. As you can clearly see.
Humans and Berlaur working hand in hand. I knew it would be possible, and now? It's real. It's here. And it's all thanks to you.
Friends, it was not long ago-
The Moonscale! It's been corrupted!
What?
A foul mist comes from the shrine, and it has been locked! There are human footprints!
"Did you see anyone back there?"
I just saw two humans running from here, they wore blue and gold clothing-
"Sounds like House Bathory."
This is Lyceon's fault! For trusting humans, for letting them in! Lyceon must step down as pack leader!
I will step down, Costas! But the Moonscale comes first. To House Bathory! Recover the key at any cost!
Thank you. Purifying the Moonscale is more important than you can imagine.
"What will happen to you?"
I must step down as leader of Umbra Clan. Costas will take my place. But you have done much for us, Soulwarden. Would you join our clan?
"I would be honored."
No! Lyceon has no power to invite anyone to our tribe, let alone a human. I don't allow it.
We will allow it. The Soulwarden has done our clan, and our entire race, a great service. Let them earn their place among us if they wish.
Bah. As long as Lyceon submits to tribunal, it is enough I suppose.
Soulwarden, can we talk privately? This is beyond impossible.
After all that my father's done for this tribe. Something's very fishy about all this. And I'll bet that bastard Costas is the one wearing the scales.
"There must be something we can do."
Yes, but carefully. Costas is watching you. Keep building your renown with the tribe. Aster and I will reach out if we find anything suspicious.
Human. Think carefully before words come out of your maw.
"Where are Nocturne and Aster?"
In a cage, where they belong. They spoke against the pack.
"You mean they spoke against you?"
"I thought you were the pack."
Speaking against me is speaking against the pack. I AM the pack. I am Apex. I am Alpha. Unlike Lyceon, I rule the pack by tooth and claw.
You test my patience! Begone before I throw you in the cage with your friends!
Still here?
Go away. Costas say it. Nobody to go into shrine.
"Costas said I should move the prisoners."
No. Costas say nobody to go into shrine, and no tell anyone about prisoners inside.
Ah! You are here. You have a soothing effect. I feel relief when I see your face.
"Costas isn't great."
He is obssessed with being Alpha! He controls through fear. He sows suspicion, distrust. And his ideas? Now he wants an "Apex feast."
"What's an Apex feast?"
"For the pack to celebrate their new Alpha." I cannot sleep. And now he has imprisoned Aster and Nocturne.
"How do I talk to them?"
I do not know. Costas has the key. And even if you had it, there are guard shifts on the shrine. Even during the celebration, someone would notice-
"We could make them fall asleep."
Yes. That could work. Perhaps my sleeping draught. But no, that would not be right. No, best we forget that idea, Soulwarden.
This juice tasty.
Toug take nap.
Soulwarden! What news of my father? Is he-
"That's what I came here to ask you."

You wonder. My assistant's notes. This place that bears knowledge of True Seeing. How long have I known you would come seeking? Hm hm.
You may not like what you saw, but the ritual only shows what is true.
Can one truly separate from the pain of empathy? It is my life's challenge.
Imagine a very large empty chamber. Fill it with piles of with rotting garbage. Now set it all ablaze. That is how my day is going, thank you very much.
How's my hair hm? Sorry did you need something?
Isn't it funny. Stuff us in these suits, and soon enough, we start to believe we belong in it.
Rupert and Sarah are so gloomy, they're like- gloomy frowny clouds. Fabian's different, his hair is like a shiny button. Oh. Did you want something?
"Slumber, sleeper, soaked dream-deep in sweet nectar of forgetfulness." The Sage King. Now. Things to do, people to assassinate, let's get to it.
Just remember, I'll be watching.
Excellent work. I wonder if you'd consider joining House Carmilla someday. Ah ah, don't need to answer now, just think on it.
I easily untangle complex weaves of power. I can spot political weakness at a glance. And yet gardening eludes me. That was levity.
To think it was Lord Galbrion, after all. There are yet strings behind that vapid narcissist, to be sure. And who will we follow them to? To me, perhaps?
It's nice to wrap up a mystery. But don't let your guard down. I've a feeling that all of this was just an opening move.
Ugh. Really, "Feeders" is an apt name for those monsters. It feels as if part of you is being consumed, and there's nothing you can do to stop it.
Buried in books in the Archives, I was able to imagine we were the same. This makes it painfully clear we're not. Humans are nothing to the Upyr.
When I say "Archives," I hope you aren't thinking of that grubby little collection managed by that servile toady Lord Varlaam. I'm from the true Archives.
This space has always fascinated me on the rare occasion we Scholars are allowed to visit. It was here long before the Upyr. The castle was built around it.
I'm sure this is all a terribly bad dream, and I'll wake up in the Archives. Pinching didn't work, and no more of that. I don't like bodily contact, even with myself.
I knew it'd be difficult, dealing with the "old guard" that supported my father. But I'd no idea they would move so boldly against me. I'll make them regret that.
Have you seen how Lynette sidles up to Lord Galbrion? Well I have. It reminds me too much of things I'd rather forget.
This place is- out of place, out of time. Always given me the shivers, like someone- or something, is watching. Let's be on our way as soon as we can.
You keep surprising me, Soulwarden. Keep it up and you'll land a spot in my royal guard. I'm joking, I'm sure you have better things to do than watch over me.
I'm grateful to have friends like you. My father warned me the most lonely place you'll ever visit is the throne.
Carmilla seems to think there's someone else yet behind the fly we're about to trap. Is one fly in the soup, better than two? Depends what's on your spoon.
Our enemies are showing their desperation, given the number of assassins they sent. Concentrate on Galbrion, we'll take care of the rest.
I almost wish for more trouble so I could see you more often. Be careful what you ask for, right?
Gisiv Yolliw Zigozih Rih Zi Nizik…
(Sabine doesn't speak but stares at you as if appealing for help.)
Werebeasts. What good are they? They certainly aren't pleasant to look at. And the smell! Simply awful.
Ugh, those boars- you'd think they would bury their excrement like any other beast, but no, they just leave it laying about! We must eradicate all of them!
Have a word with Cecilia, would you? Leaving me, the Great Lord Galbrion, out here, in this carnival of unkempt monkeys! It is a waste of talent!
Go on, judge me like everyone else, being Galbrion's shoe-kisser. I don't like the way he treats us, either! But it won't help any of us to upset the Upyr.
I get under Cecilia's skin on purpose. She needs someone to toughen her up. She might not see it that way now, but I'm on her side.
In Nighthaven, hope is the only thing we humans can truly call our own. Have to pry it out of my dead hands. The way things are going, perhaps that'll be undead.
Things appear daunting, until they don't. Keep at it, Soulwarden, I believe in you.
Ah, Everard. How could things have come to this? I never should have let him work for me. Always knew it was a stupid idea, but he insisted. Go on, now.
House Carmilla's issued Challenge! I can't believe it. We're so close now, so close.
Soulwarden. If I start yelling in the streets that miracles can happen, I blame you. With this we'll find out who's behind all this. And I'll make them pay.
The only danger about this plan is, I might just jump on whoever shows up and stab them in the neck. Not a bad thing, really.
With this, Cecilia has at least a chance of staying in power. Humans will have a better chance at being treated more fairly. But it's not enough. Not nearly.
You are interesting. I like you. I want to- ahh, I want to strap you down and slice you up, and shoot you, stab you, burn you, over and over again.
If it isn't the clown, making a little circus.
I AM TOUG! (I am angry, and I think this trial is a mockery. I am also quite hungry having eaten a light breakfast.)
Every time I think I'm done with you, you come around saving my hide again. That's a compliment in the guise of complaint. My specialty.
One day we'll have to brew a jug of lionberry juice and watch the stars together. Ah, not the kind you made before, though, please.
(The statue seems to be pointedly ignoring you.)
Hey hey hey hey! You're stepping all over my hydrangeas! Or was it- marshmallows. Marshmallows. Why!
No pie for you!
For the hundredth time, no I will not bake any birds, nor rats, into the pies!
Oh- oh my apologies, I thought you were one of these- fine revelers. Well what do you want, do I not look busy to you?
"See anyone dragged through here?"
Oh. They your friends? The Baroness wasn't very happy with those two. Hauled them to her quarters for a "chat." Healthier to stay away, if you ask me.
"What?"
Huzzah! Forget about the rest! The Upyr are the best! At least, when it's your turn for the- feedings. The Upyr are the best!
The towers that are corrupting lunar energy are the handiwork of Baroness Anastasia, an Upyr sorceress from House Bathory. She's been a real thorn in our side.
Lyceon is weak, look no further for the cause of these problems!
The Moonscale is the most sacred treasure of our people. Pulled from the very mouth of one of the Great Ones in ages past. For this to happen. Shame.
Out of my way, human.
Humans and Berlaur, only time will tell this tale.
I said it's impossible but really this makes me piping mad. How can they do this to him?
Time, sight, sound, all combine in the mists of Ancient times.
At some point in distant past, the magics of the Carnival merge with ours.
Witchcraft. Who can believe this.
We all know who the traitor is. Lyceon.
I don't usually agree with this kind of thing, but if there's a chance for hope I'll take it.
Anything I can do for Lyceon, I will.
There is always some form of hope. But in these dark times, one can forget to remember.
What madness is this? My head is swimming with all the ways things can and will go wrong.
(The vision flickers on the water.)
(The ritual knife and the Fortune Mother are gone, but not far. You can faintly hear her arguing with Aster outside the warren.)
